sn35.53:1.2: Then a certain bhikkhu approached the Blessed One, paid homage to him, sat down to one side, and said to him:
sn35.53:1.3: “Venerable sir, how should one know, how should one see, for ignorance to be abandoned and true knowledge to arise?”
sn35.53:2.1: “Bhikkhu, when one knows and sees the eye as impermanent, ignorance is abandoned and true knowledge arises. When one knows and sees forms as impermanent …
sn35.53:2.14: When one knows and sees as impermanent whatever feeling arises with mind-contact as condition—whether pleasant or painful or neither-painful-norpleasant—ignorance is abandoned and true knowledge arises.
sn35.53:2.15: When one knows and sees thus, bhikkhu, ignorance is abandoned and true knowledge arises.”
